title: A Parson’s Holiday
subtitle: Being an Account of a Tour in India, Burma, and Ceylon, in the Winter of 1882–83

summary: W. Osborn B. Allen, vicar of Shirburn in Oxfordshire and the son of a member of the Legislative Council of India, spent the winter of 1882–83 touring India, Burma, and Ceylon, and published this account of it in 1885 from what his preface calls a parson’s standpoint. He goes out by Brindisi and the P. and O. steamer to Bombay, Poona, and Rajputana, then to Delhi, Agra, Cawnpore and Lucknow, Benares, Darjeeling, and Calcutta; by sea to Rangoon, Prome, and Moulmein; and back to Madras and the south, Mysore, Trichinopoly, Madura, and the mission villages of Tinnevelly, ending in Ceylon at Colombo, Kandy, and Anuradhapura. He looks closely at missions, schools, native clergy, and the religions he meets, with long passages on Buddhism in Burma; there are also histories of places, and the return to England is by Egypt. A folding map of India and Ceylon shows the route.
